title: Investigate misattributed tokens with parallel stream merges and fallbacks
creator: Diego Ramos
description:
Summary:
We are seeing sporadic billing discrepancies reported by customers using multiplexed streaming clients and bursty batched requests. Symptoms include: duplicate token credits on reconnects, lost input tokens on mid-stream model failover, and negative-cost reconciliation adjustments from downstream aggregation jobs. These errors surface primarily for interleaved sessions that: (1) merge multiple logical streams onto a single transport connection, (2) perform in-flight model variant fallbacks, or (3) rely on the edge gateway to perform request-level batching and fan-in.

Observed behavior and repro notes:
- Reproducer created for multiplexed client that sends two logical chats (A & B) interleaved over a single websocket. On simulated gateway backpressure and reconnect, final accounting credits both A and B for some overlapping prefix tokens.
- When a midstream model fallback triggers (heavy load -> smaller quantized variant), token attribution in the aggregator sometimes assigns generation tokens to the pre-fallback model run while input credits are attributed to the post-fallback run causing misaligned per-model cost reporting and causing downstream proration bugs.
- Edge case with batched request merging: the gateway concatenates small prompts into a batch for kernel-level efficiency but fails to persist mapping metadata for batch->origin mapping when a subsequent async fragmentation occurs. This leads to orphaned fragments later reattached to the wrong session id.

Initial hypotheses for root causes:
1) Fragment identifiers are not globally unique across gateway batching + reconnect flows; collision leads to attribution mixups when fragments are re-sequenced.
2) Checkpoint snapshots that the metering service uses to finalize credits are occasionally stale due to clock skew between gateway and aggregator (see ENG-314159).
3) Idempotency/nonce scheme at the transport layer is insufficiently granular for partial-frame replays; retries reuse the same nonce resulting in double-crediting in reconciliation windows.

Proposed fixes and trade-offs:
- Implement per-fragment deterministic UUIDs scoped by (session_id, monotonic_frame_counter, origin_instance) to avoid collisions. Trade-off: small increase in metadata size per frame; benefit: deterministic attribution.
- Introduce watermarked checkpoints at aggregator ingress that include last-processed-offset and a hash of origin mappings. On reconnect, gateway must present last-synced watermark for safe resume. Trade-off: requires minor gateway change and adds a small roundtrip for resume logic; benefit: eliminates many race conditions.
- Harden idempotency tokens: move to (session_nonce, sequence_number, fragment_digest) instead of session_nonce-only. Benefit: prevents replay double-crediting.
- Persist batch origin map at time of batching to the durable mapping store (short-lived TTL 2h). If mapping store unavailable, fall back to conservative per-request billing (higher cost but correct). Trade-off: cost of extra writes; benefit: correctness under partial failures.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for fragment UUID and idempotency token generation.
- Integration test harness to simulate: interleaved streams, gateway reconnect, midstream model fallbacks, and async fragment recomposition. Add deterministic random seeds to surface race conditions repeatedly.
- Add e2e metering audit test that runs in CI against a local aggregator and verifies that per-session sum(input_tokens+output_tokens) == final_billed_tokens across 1000 random interleaving scenarios.
- Canary rollout with telemetry knobs: enable detailed attribution logging for 1% of production traffic and feed to a new reconciliation job to detect divergences vs baseline.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge generator & aggregator changes behind feature flags.
2) Deploy gateway patch that emits fragment UUID + watermark on resume. Start in staging.
3) Enable mapping store replication and TTL in a small canary cluster.
4) Activate canary detailed logging (1%) and run reconciliation job for 48h. Monitor billing delta and customer error telemetry.
5) If stable, ramp to 10% then 100% across regions.

Monitoring and alerting:
- New SLO: percent of sessions with final billing delta > 0.1% after reconciliation. Create grafana panel and alert if >0.2% for 30m.
- Reconciliation job emits daily report of orphaned fragments, duplicate-credit events, and mapping-store misses.

Open questions and decisions needed:
- Should mapping store be strongly consistent or eventual? Strong consistency simplifies correctness but increases latency on the hot path. Recommendation: use local primary + async cross-region replication to balance both.
- TTL for mapping entries: proposal 2 hours; need PM input based on longest expected reconnect window for enterprise customers.
